arxiv-1905-00570.title: Sherry H.F. Yan, Yao Yu, Hao Zhou
arxiv-1905-00570.description: Abstract On self-conjugate (s,s+1,\ldots,s+k) -core partitions Abstract. Simultaneous core partitions have been widely studied since Anderson’s work on the enumeration of (s,t) -core partitions. Amdeberhan and Leven showed that the number of (s,s+1,\ldots,s+k) -core partitions is equal to the number of (s,k) -Dyck paths.

arxiv-2104-05847.title: Targeted Adversarial Training for Natural Language Understanding
arxiv-2104-05847.creator: Lis Pereira, Xiaodong Liu, Hao Cheng, Hoifung Poon, Jianfeng Gao, Ichiro Kobayashi
arxiv-2104-05847.description: Abstract We present a simple yet effective T argeted A dversarial T raining ( TAT ) algorithm to improve adversarial training for natural language understanding. The key idea is to introspect current mistakes and prioritize adversarial training steps to where the model errs the most.

arxiv-2312-10334.title: ”SNe Ia twins for life” towards a precise determination of H 0
arxiv-2312-10334.creator: P. Ruiz-Lapuente, J.I. González Hernández
arxiv-2312-10334.description: Abstract Here we present an approach to the measurement of extragalactic distances using twin SNe Ia, taken from the early down to the nebular phase. The approach is purely empirical, although we can give a theoretical background on why the method is reliable.

arxiv-2406-17946.title: The Glow of Axion Quark Nugget Dark Matter: (II) Galaxy Clusters
arxiv-2406-17946.creator: Julian S. Sommer, Klaus Dolag, Ludwig M. Böss, Ildar Khabibullin, Xunyu Liang, Ludovic Van Waerbeke, Ariel Zhitnitsky, Fereshteh Majidi, Jenny G. Sorce, Benjamin Seidel, Elena Hernández-Martínez
arxiv-2406-17946.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Julian S. Sommer, Klaus Dolag, Ludwig M. Böss, Ildar Khabibullin, Xunyu Liang, Ludovic Van Waerbeke, Ariel Zhitnitsky, Fereshteh Majidi, Jenny G. Sorce, Benjamin Seidel, Elena Hernández-Martínez. The existence of axion quark nuggets is a potential consequence of the axion field, which provides a possible solution to the charge-conjugation parity violation in quantum chromodynamics.

arxiv-2408-06928.title: Constructing reflection-symmetric flexible realisations of graphs
arxiv-2408-06928.creator: Sean Dewar, Georg Grasegger, Jan Legerský
arxiv-2408-06928.description: Abstract We study reflection-symmetric realisations of symmetric graphs in the plane that allow a continuous symmetry and edge-length preserving deformation. To do so, we identify a necessary combinatorial condition on graphs with reflection-symmetric flexible realisations. This condition is based on a specific type of edge colouring, where edges are assigned one of three colours in a symmetric way.

arxiv-2410-12539.title: Counterfactual Effect Decomposition in Multi-Agent Sequential Decision Making
arxiv-2410-12539.creator: Stelios Triantafyllou, Aleksa Sukovic, Yasaman Zolfimoselo, Goran Radanovic
arxiv-2410-12539.description: Abstract We address the challenge of explaining counterfactual outcomes in multi-agent Markov decision processes. In particular, we aim to explain the total counterfactual effect of an agent’s action on the outcome of a realized scenario through its influence on the environment dynamics and the agents’ behavior.

pmc-10646724.title: Patient Usage of Apps to Access Online Medical Records
pmc-10646724.creator: Wesley Barker, Chelsea Richwine
pmc-10646724.description: This cross-sectional study analyzes the use of patient portal apps and third-party apps for managing multiple patient portals between 2019 and 2022. Introduction US health care’s rapid digitization over the past decade has enabled broad patient electronic access to their online medical records.1 The federal government facilitated this access through the certification of electronic health records (EHRs).

pmc-11426538.title: Unlocking the secrets of green semiotics: The revolutionary power of eco-symbols in transforming consumer perceptions and catalyzing behavioral shifts in emerging markets
pmc-11426538.creator: Wongsatorn Worakittikul, Chatrawee Saenwerm, Phaninee Naruetharadhol
pmc-11426538.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study delves into the intriguing dynamics between green semiotics and brand experiences, examining how elements like color, image, logo, and font not only shape brand experiences towards eco-friendly products but also influence green consumer behavior and thinking. Conducting a survey among 357 Thai consumers, this research uses Covariance-based Structural Equation Modeling (CB-SEM) to unearth the complex relationships between these semiotic elements and the multifaceted dimensions of brand experience—cognitive, sensory, emotional, and cultural.

pmc-11690519.title: SOCIO-EMOTIONAL DEVELOPMENT ACROSS ADULTHOOD AND AGING
pmc-11690519.creator: Urmimala Ghose, Denis Gerstorf, Jutta Heckhausen
pmc-11690519.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Understanding how social relations evolve across adulthood, thereby shaping well-being in later life is a longstanding question in lifespan developmental research. The presented studies offer novel insights, utilizing innovative methodologies, diverse time scales, and varied samples. Chopik combined qualitative data from the Harvard Student Study Class of 1964 with machine learning techniques, reporting a larger and closer friends’ circle during freshman year to be associated with more positive life reflections, enhanced relationships, and reduced mental illness fifty years later.

pmc-12751431.title: Excess of infection with SARS-CoV-2 during the first versus second wave of the COVID-19 pandemic among patients with long COVID
pmc-12751431.creator: Charles Ouazana Vedrines, Clément Gouraud, Marc Scherlinger, Sabrina Betouche, Fabrice Carrat, Eric Caumes, Victor Pitron, Olivier Robineau, Jean Sibilia, Patricia Thoreux, Kewei Xiang, Brigitte Ranque, Cédric Lemogne, CASPer-COVID study group
pmc-12751431.description: BackgroundPost-COVID-19 condition affects up to 10% of patients months after a COVID-19 episode. Population-based epidemiology suggests that self-reported long COVID in France might be more common among those infected during the first wave of the pandemic than the second one, supporting the role of contextual risk factors in symptom persistence in some patients.

pmc-13279466.title: Association of Polygenic Risk Scores With Aortic Valve Calcium: The Multi‐Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis
pmc-13279466.creator: Seamus P Whelton, Jie Yao, Clary Clish, Alexis C Wood, Kent D Taylor, Michael J Blaha, Matthew Budoff, Natalie Marrero, George Thanassoulis, Wendy S Post, Xiuqing Guo, Jerome I Rotter
pmc-13279466.description: BackgroundAortic valve calcification (AVC) is the primary process leading to aortic stenosis. We examined whether polygenic risk scores (PRS) are associated with AVC beyond traditional atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk factors.MethodsWe included 6812 participants in MESA (Multi‐Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) with computed tomography‐measured AVC at Visit 1. Using previously published PRS we calculated weighted PRS, standardized within each ancestry group.

pmc-13471598.title: Latent profile analysis identifying symptom clusters of fatigue, sleep disturbance, pain, and anxiety and their associations with health-related quality of life and self-efficacy in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13471598.creator: Yiting Zeng, Dandan Zhang, Yuzhen Fang, Mingyi Xiao, Chaona Ji, Xisui Chen
pmc-13471598.description: BackgroundPeritoneal dialysis patients experience a high burden of co-occurring symptoms that impair health-related quality of life and self-efficacy. This study applied latent profile analysis to identify distinct symptom profiles of fatigue, sleep disturbance, pain, and anxiety and to examine factors associated with profile membership and their associations with patient-reported outcomes.
